paper.title: The Pareto-optimal Trade-off between Regret and Statistical Inference in Linear Stochastic Bandits under Safety Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Safety-constrained linear bandit: estimation error under regret and safety budgets (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is the L2 estimation error E||theta_hat - theta*||_2 of the unknown parameter, subject to regret O(T^beta) and cumulative expected cost violation O(delta_T)
Each arm has an unknown stochastic cost with mean c_a; cumulative expected cost constraint E[sum_t sum_a Z_t(a) pi_t(a)] <= 0
Regret measured against the best safe static mixed policy pi* = argmax{<pi,mu> : <pi,c> <= 0}
settings.definition_quote: Consider the safety-constrained linear bandit setup with fixed action set X = {x_a}_{a in [K]} and known subGaussian parameter σ. An environment ν is fully characterized by the pair (θ*, c) of the parameter vector and the expected cost vector

settings.name_in_paper: Safety-constrained linear bandit: Phase I statistical estimation and safety
unmapped: Objective is the L2 estimation error of the unknown parameter theta* (and the cumulative safety cost incurred)
Each arm has an unknown stochastic cost Z_t(a) with mean c_a, almost surely bounded by Z_bar; cumulative expected cost constraint
The learner knows the cost bounds Z_bar and c_bar (used in the tuning of zeta_t through B(i))
settings.definition_quote: we assume that pulling arm a ∈ [K] at time t incurs a stochastic cost Z_t(a), which is an independent random variable with a (possibly unknown) mean c_a ∈ R, and consider the following cumulative safety constraint ... C(τ) := E[sum_{t=1}^τ sum_a Z_t(a)π_t(a)] ≤ 0

settings.name_in_paper: Safety-constrained linear stochastic bandit: regret minimization (Phase II / end-to-end)
unmapped: Each arm has an unknown stochastic cost Z_t(a) with mean c_a, almost surely bounded by Z_bar; cumulative expected cost constraint
Regret measured against best safe static mixed policy pi* = argmax{<pi,mu>: <pi,c> <= 0}
Slater condition with margin delta (a policy with <pi,c> <= -delta exists); the learner knows delta (V_t = delta sqrt(t))
settings.definition_quote: we assume that the true parameter vector θ* and the feature vectors x_j are uniformly bounded, such that ∥θ*∥2 ≤ S and ∥x_j∥2 ≤ L for all j ∈ [K]. ... Assumption 4.6 (Slater's Assumption). There exists a constant δ ∈ (0, 1) such that P(δ) is feasible

algorithms.name: SERMiSC (Statistical Estimation and Regret Minimization under Safety Constraint)

symbols.sigma_prime: noise standard deviation constant of the hard instances (independent of T)
symbols.C_reg: constant in the regret budget R(T) <= C_reg T^beta

conditions: policies in Π(β, δ_T): R(T) = O(T^β) and C(T) = O(δ_T)
infimum over all estimators of theta*

source.quote: Then there exist constants σ′, C > 0 (independent of T) such that inf_{π ∈ Π(β,δT), θ̂} sup_{ν ∈ V} E^π_ν ∥θ̂ − θ*_ν∥2 ≥ 5σ′ / (2 sqrt(δT + 10CT^β)).

results.notes: Minimax lower bound on the L2 estimation error over the class of algorithms with regret O(T^beta) and safety violation O(delta_T). The proof also gives a probability lower bound via KL; only the expectation bound is recorded.

symbols.q: inf_t q_t > 0, lower bound on the exploration mixing weight
symbols.tr_design: tr((sum_i pi'(i) x_i x_i^T)^{-1}) for the exploratory policy pi'

conditions: theta* in a bounded set B_theta (estimator projected onto it)
tuning: q = inf_t q_t > 0 constant independent of T_1

source.quote: Let θ̂ denote the estimator produced by Phase I of the SERMiSC algorithm in Algorithm 1, with the hyperparameter sequence {qt}t≥1 chosen such that q := inf t≥1 qt > 0 is a constant independent of T1. Then, ∃t0 ∈ N such that for any T1 ≥ t0, it holds that E||θ̂ − θ*||2 ≤ sqrt(11σ²/(9qT1) tr((Σ π′(i)xi xi^⊤)^{-1})) = O(T1^{-1/2}).

results.notes: Estimation error of the OLS estimator after Phase I.

conditions: Assumption 4.2: max_a c_a < c_bar, |c_min| >= varsigma c_bar, Z_t(a) <= Z_bar a.s.

source.quote: Set ζt as in (4). Then, under Assumption 4.2, ∃t1 ∈ N such that for any T1 ≥ t1, it holds that ∆C1(T1) ≤ 2 Σ_{i≠imin ∧ ci>0} ci [2K Σ(1−qt)]^{D/(D+1)} [(1−q)(1+2/W(i)²)]^{1/(D+1)} ... by choosing D = 1/ln T1, we obtain ... ∆C1(T1) = O((ln T1)²).

results.notes: Bound on the additional safety cost ΔC1 (cost beyond the reference mixture of π' and the cheapest arm) in Phase I; the general D-dependent expression is not recorded.

source.quote: Suppose Assumption 4.2 holds. By setting qt = ς/(1+ς) for all t ∈ [T1] and letting π′ be the uniform distribution (i.e., π′ = (1/K)1), the expected safety cost satisfies: C1(T1) ≤ ∆C1(T1) = O((ln T1)²).

results.notes: Cumulative expected safety cost (constraint violation) of Phase I.

conditions: Assumption 4.6 (Slater condition with margin delta in (0,1))

source.quote: Let R2(τ) be the cumulative regret incurred during Phase II of the SERMiSC algorithm in Algorithm 2 over the period from time 1 + T1 to τ ≤ T. Under Assumption 4.6, by setting Vt = δ√t, ϵt = 4/√t, and ϱ = 1/T, it holds that R2(T2) ≤ 4 + 16 ... + λS ... sqrt(2T2 log(1 + T2L²/(λd))), which implies an asymptotic upper bound of R2(T2) = Õ(√T(1/δ + 1/δ³)).

results.notes: The explicit bound is garbled by PDF extraction; the asymptotic form is recorded following the appendix (Õ(√T/δ + 1/δ³)). The main text form may read Õ(√T(1/δ + 1/δ³)); uncertainty about placement of the sqrt(T) factor. Regret is against the best safe static mixed policy, defined through means.

source.quote: Let C2(τ) be the safety cost incurred during Phase II ... Under Assumption 4.6, by setting Vt = δ√t, ϵt = 4/√t, and ϱ = 1/T, it holds that C2(T2) ≤ 8 + ((Z̄+4)²+(Z̄+4)δ/24)/(δ/8) log(1 + (16(Z̄+4)²+2(Z̄+4)δ/3)/(δ²/8)) + (1+⌈64/δ²⌉)(Z̄+4) + 4(Z̄²+16)/δ, implying that the safety cost remains O(1) relative to T2.

results.notes: Cumulative safety constraint violation in Phase II; independent of T2.

source.quote: Let β ∈ [1/2, 1), T1 = ⌊T^β⌋, and T2 = T − T1. Under Assumptions 4.2 and 4.6, with the parameter choices specified in Section 4, the SERMiSC algorithm simultaneously achieves: (Regret) R(T) = Õ(T1 + √T2) = Õ(T^β), (Safety) C(T) = Õ(1), (Estimation) err(T) = O(T^{−β/2}).

results.notes: End-to-end regret; dependence on Slater margin suppressed.
Estimation error; matches the lower bound of Theorem 3.1 with delta_T = Õ(1), up to logarithmic factors.
